rule: The minor axis of an ellipse points along the axis perpendicular to the circle's surface, like the axle of a wheel.
To draw a circle in perspective get the minor axis right first, then the degree of the ellipse.
The silhouette line is drawn tangent to all the section lines of the volume.
Where one line overlaps another, the overlapping foreground line is drawn thicker.
Linear perspective, occlusion and atmospheric perspective (lower contrast with distance) are the depth cues that translate to drawing.
A 60 degree cone of vision, close to a 50mm lens, gives an acceptable, natural-looking amount of distortion.
